title_key: beyond comprehension|hajji
title: Beyond comprehension
abstract: The rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence in educational contexts has transformed how students encounter academic content, yet a fundamental question remains underexamined: Do English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners possess the critical literacy competencies needed to evaluate AI-generated texts? This study investigated whether students in Morocco’s Classes Préparatoires aux Grandes Écoles (CPGE)—one of the nation’s most academically selective post-secondary programs—demonstrate readiness for AI-era literacy demands. We developed a diagnostic assessment instrument, the Critical Reading Diagnostic Assessment (CRDA), designed to mirror common characteristics of AI-generated academic content: a confident, authoritative tone, a logical structure with subtle gaps, claims requiring verification, and culturally embedded assumptions. Thirty first-year CPGE students (M age = 18.6 years) evaluated argumentative passages across five critical dimensions: argument identification, evidence evaluation, assumption recognition, multi-source synthesis, and source criticism. Metacognitive self-assessment data were also collected. Results revealed systematic evaluation failures across all dimensions, with mean accuracy rates of only 18–39% and large effect sizes confirming substantial deficits (d = 1.11–2.25). Metacognitive analysis showed that students overestimated their abilities by 11–38 percentage points across all dimensions, indicating profound self-assessment inaccuracies.

title_key: comparative evaluation of llm based configurations for a rag student counseling chatbot|nazah
title: Comparative Evaluation of LLM-Based Configurations for a RAG Student Counseling Chatbot
abstract: In higher education institutions, student counseling systems face difficulties in providing context-aware, empathetic, and institution-specific responses through standard intent-based architecture. To solve this, a comparative evaluation was conducted on two configurations of an AI persona student counseling chatbot developed at Bina Insani University. The baseline configuration utilizes Gemini 2.5 Flash, rule-based routing, and a FAISS vector database with a Top-K retrieval depth of 3. The enhanced configuration implements Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, an LLM-based context judge directing queries into four discrete routes, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Top-K set to 5, and route-specific structured prompt engineering. Both pipelines process Bina Insani University institutional documents split into five categories using the multilingual-e5-small embedding model with 800-character chunk sizes, 150-character overlap, and a 0.80 cosine similarity threshold. Evaluation using Llama 3.3 70B Versatile across 45 test scenarios yielded an overall average quality score of 4.48 for the enhanced system compared to 4.475 for the baseline. Specifically, the enhanced system improved general empathy from 4.53 to 4.80 and campus service answer relevance from 4.50 to 4.80, though RAG faithfulness dropped from 4.62 to 4.33. Expert validation by a university counselor rated both systems 100% suitable across all 45 test scenarios, while User Acceptance Testing with 20 students showed an increase in overall satisfaction from 91% to 93%. Higher education administrators and conversational AI developers can deploy LLM-based routing and pgvector architectures to deliver flexible, less repetitive, and category-optimized automated counseling support.

title_key: active learning with generative ai in introductory physics a multi institutional study of the p a i r framework|paul
title: Active Learning with Generative AI in Introductory Physics: A Multi-Institutional Study of the P-A.I.R. Framework
abstract: Generative AI tools have become part of how students study physics, yet unstructured use may reduce students'opportunities to work through problems independently. The Physics AI-Replication (P-A.I.R.) framework structures AI use as a four-step cycle: students identify a challenging problem, obtain an AI-generated explanation and solution, request similar practice problems, and solve them independently before reviewing the AI's solutions. We evaluated P-A.I.R. in 11 algebra- and calculus-based introductory physics sections at four U.S. institutions using a common end-of-semester survey. Most students reported improved conceptual understanding (90.9\%) and found the replicated practice problems helpful (97.7\%), and these two ratings were strongly associated ($r_s = 0.58$). Perceptions of both components, as well as post-engagement confidence ($\mu = 7.18$ on a 1-10 scale), were consistent across institutions. Post-engagement confidence was associated with perceived improvement in conceptual understanding ($r_s = 0.37$) and the helpfulness of replicated practice ($r_s = 0.35$), but not with how often students used AI ($r_s = 0.02$) or with self-reported GPA ($r_s = 0.13$). Thematic analysis of open-ended responses showed that students valued AI primarily for conceptual clarification and structured problem solving (63.0\%), while their main concerns were AI accuracy (34.2\%) and the need for explanations that guide rather than simply provide answers (29.7\%). These findings suggest that how students engage with AI matters more than how often they use it, and that frameworks sequencing AI assistance with independent problem solving offer a practical, transferable approach for physics instruction.

title_key: student engagement and trust calibration with generative ai in a 5s safety assessment|sharifuzzaman
title: Student Engagement and Trust Calibration With Generative AI in a 5S Safety Assessment
abstract:
Generative AI is increasingly used in engineering and technology education, but its role in safety education remains underexplored. This study examined undergraduate students’ (
 N
  = 14) human-AI interaction during a 5S workplace safety assessment in a Human Factors course. Using a mixed-methods design, we analyzed User Engagement Scale–Short Form (UES-SF) responses and qualitative reflections after students independently completed a hazard identification task and compared findings with a parallel AI-generated assessment (ChatGPT-4o). Results revealed high perceived reward and value, minimal usability barriers, and mixed focused attention, suggesting task engagement without deep immersion. Qualitatively, students described AI as expanding hazard awareness, improving analytical structure, and accelerating information retrieval, while consistently emphasizing the necessity of human oversight and cautioning against overreliance. Integrated findings position generative AI as a human-in-the-loop decision-support tool: effective for scaffolding systematic reasoning and broadening hazard recognition, but insufficient as a substitute for domain-informed judgment.
venue: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting

title_key: lcsr llm longitudinal cognitive state reasoning for llm based knowledge tracing|zhang
title: LCSR-LLM: Longitudinal Cognitive State Reasoning for LLM-based Knowledge Tracing
abstract: Knowledge tracing aims to infer a student's evolving mastery from historical learning interactions. Recent large language model (LLM) approaches offer a natural way to encode textualized learning histories, but they are often evaluated primarily as next-step predictors. This leaves open whether the model forms a stable and diagnostically meaningful latent trajectory of student state, or merely exploits shallow statistics such as recent correctness rates. We introduce LCSR-LLM, a longitudinal cognitive state reasoning framework that uses marker-aligned LLM hidden states to estimate a soft latent cognitive-state trajectory at each prediction step. The framework combines state-conditioned prediction with trajectory-level regularization, especially dynamic consistency and entropy control, to encourage smoother and non-collapsed state posteriors. We further propose Longitudinal Aggregation Drift (LAD), a diagnostic protocol that measures sequence-level prediction drift, posterior uncertainty, and trajectory volatility. On ASSIST2012, LCSR-LLM with Qwen2.5-7B reaches 0.7684 AUC, 0.7705 ACC, and 0.8610 F1, achieving the best AUC among our controlled runs and the best F1 among the listed results, while remaining competitive in ACC. Paired trajectory diagnostics show that dynamic consistency and entropy control improve internal trajectory behavior beyond final predictive accuracy.
venue: Proceedings of the 35th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management

title_key: a data engineering driven machine learning framework for efl writing performance analysis|khan
title: A Data Engineering-Driven Machine Learning Framework for EFL Writing Performance Analysis
abstract: Explainable machine learning has been applied to textual predictors of writing quality, but rarely to the behavioral and motivational predictors, feedback modality and self-regulated learning (SRL), that dominate confirmatory EFL writing research. This study analyzes a quasi-experimental, ten-week EFL writing-feedback intervention (n=84), recording feedback condition (instructor-mediated, automated, or generative-AI), proficiency, and 35-item SRL strategy use alongside pre/post analytic writing scores across six outcomes. A pre-modeling reliability check found the SRL questionnaire did not reproduce its published factor structure (Cronbach's alpha = 0.279), so a single composite served as the motivational predictor, with centered feedback-by-SRL interaction terms. Five model classes were compared under nested cross-validation with per-trait tuning. Random forest achieved the best aggregate performance (MCRMSE = 2.240, mean R² = 0.293); a stacked ensemble performed worse than its base learners on every trait (mean R² = −0.344). A fixed-hyperparameter baseline outperformed the nested-CV-tuned pipeline (MCRMSE 2.197 vs. 2.258), showing tuning, not feature engineering, degraded performance here. SHAP attribution identified feedback condition, especially generative-AI feedback, as the dominant predictor for all six outcomes, with feedback-by-SRL interactions outweighing SRL's own main effect on three of six traits. A multi-task neural network outperformed an equivalent single-task ensemble on every trait using 5.75 times fewer parameters. These results show explainable, cross-validated machine learning can corroborate confirmatory EFL writing findings while surfacing measurement and methodological cautions.
venue: Journal of Data Technologies and Engineering

title_key: exploring efl students use of ai tools in speaking classes purposes motivations and perceived benefits|nguyen
title: Exploring EFL Students’ Use of AI Tools in Speaking Classes: Purposes, Motivations, and Perceived Benefits
abstract: Despite the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in education, empirical evidence on how EFL learners use AI tools to improve speaking skills remains limited. This study examines the specific AI tools, usage purposes, motivations, and percieved benefits among university EFL students. A quantitative survey was administered to 155 freshmen at Ho Chi Minh City University of Industry and Trade (HUIT). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics in SPSS. The findings revealed that generative AI chatbots (notably ChatGPT and Gemini) were widely adopted, primarily for idea generation, vocabulary enrichment, and translation. Learners were motivated by perceived usefulness, ease of use, and reduced speaking anxiety. Major reported benefits include enhanced confidence, expanded vocabulary, and greater learning flexibility.  These findings offer practical insights for integrating generative AI tools into tertiary EFL speaking curricula.

title_key: using advanced digital tools for asynchronous courses delivery designed for students enrolled in public administration programs|vrabie
title: Using advanced digital tools for asynchronous courses delivery designed for students enrolled in public administration programs
abstract: The swift progression of digital tools and artificial intelligence (AI) has reshaped the educational landscape, creating both challenges and opportunities for asynchronous IT-related courses in public administration (PA) programs. For future public servants, such courses are not only vehicles for content delivery, but also spaces in which foundational competencies such as digital literacy, problem-solving, autonomous learning, and the effective use of technology in administrative contexts can be strengthened. This article outlines a framework for improving professor–student interaction and asynchronous course delivery, drawing on institutional research and relevant e-learning literature. It reports the outcomes of a university research project aimed at personalizing learning experiences through visual technologies, gamification, and AI-supported assistance, with particular attention to one introductory computer science course. The article presents an exploratory comparison of three naturally occurring cohorts of students in three consecutive academic years, examining how the staged integration of gamification and a GPT-4–based assistant coincided with changes in academic performance. The results show performance improvements across cohorts exposed to increasingly innovative delivery approaches. In a quasi-experimental comparison, exam performance improved following the staged introduction of gamification and AI-supported assistance, while the findings also suggest the broader pedagogical relevance of such tools for preparing PA students for digitally mediated professional environments.

title_key: influence the use of artificial intelligence ai against ability think critical accounting education study program students state university of medan|sembiring
title: Influence The Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Against Ability Think Critical Accounting Education Study Program Students State University of Medan
abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly ChatGPT, use on the critical thinking skills of students in the Accounting Education Study Program at Universitas Negeri Medan. This study employed a quantitative approach with a correlational research design and simple linear regression analysis. The population consisted of 308 active students from the 2022–2025 cohorts, with a sample of 116 students from the 2025 cohort selected using random sampling. Data were collected through a closed-ended questionnaire using a three-point Likert scale, consisting of 24 items measuring AI use and 24 items measuring critical thinking skills. The research instrument was tested for validity and reliability, and all items were found to be valid and reliable. The results showed that AI use had a positive and statistically significant effect on students’ critical thinking skills. This was indicated by a calculated t-value of 6.581, which was greater than the critical t-value of 1.658 at the 5% significance level. The resulting regression equation was Y = 29.027 + 0.496X, with a coefficient of determination of 27.5%. This indicates that AI use explained 27.5% of the variance in students’ critical thinking skills, while the remaining 72.5% was influenced by other factors beyond the scope of this study. Based on the categorization results, the majority of students were classified in the moderate category for both AI use (64.66%) and critical thinking skills (65.52%). Therefore, students’ use of ChatGPT can be considered relatively adequate but still needs to be optimized to support the development of their critical thinking skills.

title_key: leveraging conversational ai for time management insights from higher education student perceptions|lim
title: Leveraging Conversational AI for Time Management: Insights From Higher Education Student Perceptions
abstract: Effective time management is essential for academic success in higher education, particularly as students navigate increasingly complex and autonomous learning environments. However, many students continue to struggle with goal-setting, scheduling, and task prioritization, which can hinder academic performance and well-being. While conversational AI tools like chatbots have gained prominence in educational contexts, their application in supporting students’ time management remains underexplored. This study aimed to investigate higher education students’ perceptions of a conversational AI chatbot as a tool for time management. A quantitative survey design incorporating both descriptive and inferential statistics was employed, involving 187 ESL foundation students from a university in Malaysia. The instrument consisted of ten items adapted from established models, including TAM, UTAUT, and SUS, organized into three constructs: perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and behavioral intention. Construct validity and reliability were confirmed prior to analysis. Results indicated high agreement on the chatbot’s usefulness and ease of use, particularly in organizing tasks and saving time, though behavioral intention to use it regularly was comparatively moderate. Furthermore, inferential analysis confirmed that perceived ease of use and usefulness significantly predicted students’ behavioral intention. These findings suggest that while students recognize the benefits of AI for productivity, ongoing support and integration are needed to promote sustained use. The study contributes to the growing discourse on AI in education and highlights the perceived educational value of conversational agents as supportive tools for student organization and digital readiness.

title_key: evaluating students perceptions of chatgpt s effectiveness on motivation and understanding in statistics education|yanti
title: Evaluating Students' Perceptions of Chatgpt's Effectiveness on Motivation and Understanding in Statistics Education
abstract: The use of ChatGPT in higher education is growing rapidly, but empirical research on its impact on students' academic performance in Indonesia remains very limited. This quantitative and computational study predicts the perceived effectiveness of ChatGPT on students' learning motivation and conceptual understanding in a Statistics course. The study collected data from 406 active users who completed a 25-item questionnaire which used a 5-point Likert scale for their responses. The research instrument evaluates four separate constructs through its measurement of Intensity of ChatGPT Use $(V_{1})$, Ease of Use $(V_{2})$, Learning Motivation $(V_{3})$, and Impact on Learning Outcomes $(V_{4})$, which achieved a Cronbach's Alpha score above 0.91. Descriptive analysis revealed a mean score of $\bar{X}=3.582$ and an effectiveness index of 71.6%, categorizing ChatGPT as an “effective” tool. Due to a violation of the normality assumption, we used the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test to demonstrate that the obtained data significantly exceeded the neutral threshold $(W=18,654.500, p<0.05)$. Additionally, modeling using a Random Forest Classifier to predict effectiveness levels achieved a test data accuracy of 84.15% and a weighted F1 score of 82.35%. The Mean Decrease in Impurity (MDI) metric identified usage intensity $(V_{1})$ as the primary predictor of computational performance, followed by motivation and readiness to learn $(V_{3})$ and ease of use $(V_{2})$. We conclude that although ChatGPT is very useful as a learning supplement, its integration should still be combined with conventional materials to anticipate the risk of misinformation.

title_key: generative ai in higher education adoption risks and opportunities in the indian subcontinent|pinto
title: Generative AI in higher education: adoption, risks, and opportunities in the Indian subcontinent
abstract:
This study aims to investigate generative AI (GenAI) adoption in Indian Subcontinent higher education – a region marked by extreme socio-economic inequalities, infrastructural deficits and linguistic diversity – examining how perceived ease of use, usefulness, satisfaction, trust and security influence students’ continuance intention.
 
 
 
 A sequential mixed-methods design was used. Quantitative data from an online survey of higher education students (n = 704) across seven South Asian countries were analyzed using partial least squares-structural equation modelling. Qualitative data were collected via semi-structured interviews with 14 professors from six countries within the Indian Subcontinent. The Technology Continuance Theory (TCT) served as the analytical framework.
 
 
 
 Perceived ease of use, usefulness, satisfaction, trust and security significantly shape continuance intention. Satisfaction emerged as the strongest predictor of continuance intention (ß = 0.571, p < 0.001). Applications concentrate on content creation, administrative automation and performance enhancement. However, limited broadband access, chronic power instability, entrenched inequalities and underrepresentation of regional languages in large language models constrain equitable adoption.
 
 
 
 The cross-sectional design limits causal inferences. Self-reported data may introduce bias and the sample overrepresents urban, English-proficient populations. Future research should use longitudinal designs, include administrator perspectives, experimentally evaluate interventions for linguistic barriers and conduct comparative studies across Global South and North contexts.
 
 
 
 South Asian higher education institutions must address infrastructure deficits (reliable electricity, affordable internet), integrate GenAI tools with clear ethical guidelines, advocate for regional-language large language models, negotiate subsidized licenses and provide faculty development programs to bridge the generational digital divide.
 
 
 
 Without inclusive digital policies and culturally attuned regulations, GenAI risks exacerbating divides between elite urban universities and underfunded rural colleges and between English speakers and regional language users. North–South partnerships are essential for equitable and sustainable higher education in the Global South.
 
 
 
 To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is among the first to examine GenAI continuance intention across the entire Indian Subcontinent (seven countries). It extends TCT by integrating region-specific barriers – infrastructural instability, linguistic exclusion and socio-economic inequality – alongside AI-specific antecedents. The mixed-methods design provides robust, context-sensitive evidence from both students and professors.

title_key: a github proxy framework for promoting srl and student agency in software engineering capstones|lu
title: A GitHub Proxy Framework for Promoting SRL and Student Agency in Software Engineering Capstones
abstract: As generative AI becomes routine in computing education, observing students’ actual development work is becoming increasingly difficult. The critical challenge goes beyond detecting AI use to preserving student agency to ensure they learn, understand and master the code they produce. To address this, we operationalise standard GitHub traces into a two-tier framework of behavioural indicators aligned with the tenets of self-regulated learning: planning, enactment, and adaptation phases of an Agile sprint. In doing so, we surface these traces and aim to enhance students’ agency to monitor and adjust their habits, thereby actively fostering self-regulated learning. We validate these theory-driven indicators using quantitative, deterministic methods on a postgraduate capstone cohort (N = 118). Our analysis confirms the indicators demonstrate moderate cross-sprint stability and capture complementary, rather than strictly independent, behavioural patterns. Ultimately, this paper offers a pedagogical provocation: scalable trace-based analytics should pivot from instruments of assessment into pedagogical tools, generating timely, customised feedback that empowers students to critically reflect on their software development practices.

title: GENAI В АКАДЕМІЧНОМУ ПИСЬМІ: ЕМПІРИЧНЕ ДОСЛІДЖЕННЯ РЕКОНСТРУКЦІЇ КОНЦЕПТУАЛЬНИХ КОМПОНЕНТІВ НАУКОВОГО ДОСЛІДЖЕННЯ
abstract: The article addresses the topical issue of using generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in working with academic texts by combining practical work with GenAI, the analysis of dissertation abstracts, and the development of students’ critical attitudes toward AI-generated information. This study investigates the ability of generative artificial intelligence to reconstruct selected conceptual components of academic discourse without direct access to the corresponding dissertation abstract. The study analyzes contemporary scholarly approaches to the use of generative artificial intelligence in academic discourse. The aim of the study is to empirically determine the extent to which GenAI can reproduce the relevance, research aim, and research focus of an academic study based on a minimal set of input data. The methodology involved an experimental procedure with 25 undergraduate students enrolled in the program “Language and Literature (German). Translation” within the field of Germanic languages and literatures. The empirical material comprised 25 abstracts of successfully defended dissertations on Germanic linguistics. Two generative AI systems, ChatGPT and Gemini, were used in the experiment. Following a standardized prompting procedure, the systems were provided with the research topic, but the corresponding dissertation abstract was not made available to them. The AI-generated responses were compared with the corresponding conceptual components of the dissertation abstracts using comparative content analysis. The results indicate that GenAI can semantically reconstruct selected characteristics of an existing academic study, including its relevance, research aim, and focus. At the same time, the findings do not indicate textual copying of dissertation abstracts but rather suggest the possibility of reconstructing their content-related characteristics from limited input data. These results indicate the considerable potential of GenAI as a tool for supporting academic writing. Practical implications. The findings may be used to develop university curricula that establish a balanced approach to integrating generative artificial intelligence into the educational process while preserving fundamental principles of academic integrity and values.

title_key: ontology grounded neuro symbolic intelligent tutoring and knowledge assessment system supporting smart digital education|nurgazinova
title: ONTOLOGY-GROUNDED NEURO-SYMBOLIC INTELLIGENT TUTORING AND KNOWLEDGE-ASSESSMENT SYSTEM SUPPORTING SMART DIGITAL EDUCATION
abstract: Intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) for elementary algebra face a persistent tension between the interpretability of symbolic, knowledge-engineered models and the predictive power of purely neural learner models, while recent large-language-model (LLM) assistants add fluency at the cost of factual and pedagogical reliability. This paper describes an algebra tutoring system organised around a formal ontology. The ontology is an OWL knowledge base: it lists the algebraic concepts, records which concepts are prerequisites for which, and states axioms for the misconceptions students commonly hold. Both the reasoning and the assessment components read from it. Reasoning is handled by a rule-based computer-algebra solver paired with a neural knowledge-tracing model. The prerequisite relations enter the training objective as a regularisation term: the tracer is penalised when it claims a student has mastered a concept while that student still fails the prerequisites for it. Assessment uses an item-response model with ontology-weighted item parameters. Because the weights are tied to concepts, the model returns a separate mastery estimate for each concept, which is what makes the output legible to a teacher. A retrieval-augmented, ontology-constrained LLM pedagogical assistant generates hints and explanations whose vocabulary and inferences are restricted to entailments of the knowledge base, sharply reducing hallucination. The study ran for eight weeks with 428 learners. On held-out interactions the knowledge-tracing model reached an AUC of 0.851 and an RMSE of 0.369, ahead of both the Bayesian and the deep knowledge-tracing baselines. Learning gains separated the conditions more sharply than the tracing metrics did: normalized gain was (g) = 0.58 for the full system, 0.41 for a generic LLM tutor, and 0.24 for the textbook condition. Expert raters also preferred the ontology-grounded hints when asked to judge faithfulness. What this shows is narrower than it may look. A single cohort over eight weeks cannot establish that ontological grounding is what produced the gains, since the grounded system also differs from the LLM tutor in its solver and its hint templates. It does show that the combination is workable at the scale of a real course, and that grounding the hints in an explicit knowledge base does not cost accuracy in exchange for transparency.

title_key: duet rapid automated feedback for uml class diagrams and er diagrams|gurtl
title: DUET: Rapid Automated Feedback for UML Class Diagrams and ER Diagrams
abstract: Providing timely, clear, and actionable feedback is a persistent challenge in large computing courses, where feedback often arrives only after grading and is reduced to brief, rubric-oriented comments. Conceptual models such as Unified Modeling Language (UML) class diagrams and Entity-Relationship (ER) diagrams are particularly affected, as assessing them requires interpreting each student’s individual design. We present DUET, a web-based tool that provides formative feedback on conceptual models while students are still working on them. Students upload their diagrams as images, whether hand-drawn or digitally created. DUET converts them to PlantUML through a decomposed multimodal large language model (MLLM) pipeline, compares its structure against instructor-provided reference solutions, and phrases the detected differences as neutral, reflective prompts that encourage revision without revealing the solution. Students can rate each feedback message and resubmit revised diagrams for iterative feedback. Educators manage assignments and editable reference solutions. Following a design-based research approach, we refined the design through formative interviews with six educators and deployed the tool in an introductory object-oriented programming course, where 135 students voluntarily uploaded 530 UML class diagrams while preparing for a graded modeling assignment. Half of the students revised their diagram at least once in response to feedback, typically within minutes of receiving it. An evaluation of the pipeline showed that it produced feedback based on a faithful conversion of the drawing for 74% of these authentic submissions. In addition, pre-/post-surveys show that students experienced the feedback as supportive and manageable but frequently doubted its correctness, while trust in large language models (LLMs) remained unchanged and confidence in UML class diagram modeling tended to increase. Based on these findings, we discuss design lessons for integrating LLM-based diagram feedback as formative learning support, and we release the tool, its prompts, and the study data.

title_key: a context aware mobile learning framework for personalized student support using artificial intelligence|karthick
title: A Context-Aware Mobile Learning Framework for Personalized Student Support Using Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Context-aware mobile learning aims to adapt educational content not only to what a learner knows but to the situation in which learning occurs the time available, network connectivity, and time of day. Most deployed mobile-learning applications still personalize on mastery alone and ignore this situational layer, limiting real-world relevance of recommendations. This paper presents the design and implementation of an Android-based, AI-driven context-aware mobile learning framework built around a learner-model service, a context-acquisition module, and a novel context-aware linear contextual-bandit recommendation engine that jointly weighs mastery fit, time-budget fit, and connectivity fit when selecting learning activities, in contrast to prior educational bandit and collaborativefiltering approaches that condition on mastery state alone. We detail the system architecture, database schema, and recommendation algorithm with full mathematical specification, and we specify a pre-registered ten-week quasi-experimental classroom evaluation protocol. To validate the recommendation algorithm prior to classroom deployment, we conduct a controlled simulation with synthetic learners, a synthetic content catalog, and situational context sampled across thirty independent runs, extended with comparisons against established contextual-bandit baselines, feature-removal ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, and non-parametric statistical validation. The context-aware bandit achieved a mean final-window recommendation accuracy of 22.0% against a ground-truth fit criterion, significantly higher than a context-agnostic, mastery-only ablation (20.3%) and a random baseline (12.8%; paired t-tests, p < .001 for both comparisons). These simulation-based results provide initial algorithmic evidence supporting the feasibility of the proposed recommendation framework prior to real-world classroom deployment, which is specified as future work in the evaluation protocol. We conclude with a discussion of design implications, a comparison against related LLM- and bandit-based educational systems, limitations, ethical considerations, and a concrete plan for human-subject evaluation.

title_key: ai cosmos an agentic infra for situated learning|team
title: AI Cosmos: An Agentic Infra for Situated Learning
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can improve task performance during learning, yet these gains do not necessarily reflect learners'ability to thereafter apply the knowledge and skills independently. We present AI Cosmos, an agentic infrastructure for situated learning that organizes learning around two complementary principles: scenario-based participation and cumulative assets of practice. AI Cosmos organizes learners and role-specialized agents within learning scenarios that integrate task-relevant knowledge and, when needed, executable workbenches. An asset-memory loop preserves the processes and outcomes of practice as reusable assets with explicit provenance and dependencies. We evaluate scenario-based interaction through two preregistered randomized controlled studies examining the acquisition of legal reasoning and programming competence, holding the same underlying LLM across conditions. AI Cosmos achieves greater learning gains than a conventional LLM in legal reasoning and higher mastery of unseen programming problems than an LLM-as-Teacher baseline.

title_key: de la adopcion a la reflexion|pardo
title: De la adopción a la reflexión
abstract: The rise of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) is transforming reading, writing, and learning practices in higher education, which presents ethical challenges related to authorship, transparency, and critical digital literacy. In the field of initial teacher education, it is necessary to move beyond an instrumental use of these technologies and promote ethical and pedagogical reflection on their implications. This study examines the evolution of the ethical and reflective use of GAI among prospective Primary Education teachers by comparing perceptions, practices, and levels of critical awareness between first- and third-year students enrolled in a Primary Education degree program. Using a mixed-methods and comparative design, the responses of 486 students were analyzed through transparency protocols based on Cassany’s (2024) ethical model, which includes 5 dimensions: acknowledgment of GAI use, purposes of use, prompt formulation, verification of results, and critical reflection. Quantitative and qualitative findings reveal significant differences between both educational levels. While first-year students show a predominantly instrumental approach focused on textual correction and reformulation, third-year students demonstrate greater ethical and metacognitive maturity, with more diversified uses, increased verification of information, and more elaborate critical reflections. The findings suggest that critical digital competence develops progressively throughout university education and that the early introduction of ethical protocols may foster this process.

title_key: teachers emotional responses to critical incidents in digital entrepreneurial learning environments|kristanti
title: Teachers Emotional Responses to Critical Incidents in Digital Entrepreneurial Learning Environments
abstract: In the contemporary edupreneurial ecosystem, optimizing human capital and engineering adaptive Educational Technology (EdTech) architectures demand a mathematical, data-driven understanding of stakeholders' internal emotional and behavioral dynamics. This study examines how secondary school teachers depict their emotions toward critical incidents in classroom discourse by applying an advanced Systemic Functional Linguistics (SFL) appraisal framework, mapping these dynamics for structural integration into automated affective computing systems. Involving two public Islamic secondary school teachers within a boarding school environment as focal instructional assets, this investigation dissects teachers' emotions toward critical incidents, their cognitive emotion regulation strategies, and the resultant vectors of emotional understanding or misunderstanding across gendered and socio-educational strata. The empirical findings reveal that positive affect structures predominantly map the emotional architecture of the male teacher, whereas negative affect systems characterize the communicative patterns of the female teacher when navigating disruptive critical incidents. These behaviors are heavily conditioned by systemic gender roles and institutional socio-religious capital. Furthermore, while both educators leverage cognitive change (reappraisal) as an emotional regulation strategy, the male teacher operates through exclusive positive affect pathways, whereas the female teacher exhibits a dual-phase response (negative affect transitioning into positive affect), highly mediated by pedagogical tenure and experience. Crucially, the male teacher fosters sustained emotional understanding via positive inclination and happiness systems, whereas the female teacher's discourse reflects severe emotional misunderstanding, characterized by linguistic domination, discourse control, and subtle verbal oppression. This study synthesizes these socio-linguistic dimensions into an Edu-Affective Analytics Framework, presenting actionable technopreneurial recommendations for scaling empathetic AI tutors, deploying automated performance tracking matrices, and optimizing human resource workflows within modern educational enterprises.

title_key: effects of generative ai based flipped learning on self efficacy self directed learning ability metacognition and ai ethics awareness among nursing students|seo
title: Effects of Generative AI-Based Flipped Learning on Self-Efficacy, Self-Directed Learning Ability, Metacognition, and AI Ethics Awareness among Nursing Students
abstract: This study examined changes in self-efficacy, self-directed learning ability, metacognition, and AI ethics awareness after generative AI-based flipped learning. A one-group pretest-posttest pre-experimental design was used with 40 nursing students in Korea. The program included AI-based pre-class learning, collaborative in-class activities, and post-class reflection. Data were analyzed using paired t-tests and Pearson's correlation coefficients with SPSS version 25.0. All four variables significantly improved after the intervention (p < .001), and significant positive correlations were found among them. These findings suggest that generative AI-based flipped learning may be a learner-centered strategy supporting nursing students' cognitive, affective, and ethical competencies. The results provide foundational evidence for developing AI-based instructional models and digital learning environments in nursing education.

title_key: a survey on emotion aware programming assistance using large language models eye gaze analysis and keystroke dynamics|a
title: A Survey on Emotion-Aware Programming Assistance Using Large Language Models, Eye-Gaze Analysis and Keystroke Dynamics
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are entering programming education quickly, where they are used to produce hints, feedback, exercises, and code explanations. Most of these tools respond only to the code or error message in front of them and remain unaware of whether the learner is confused, frustrated, bored, or overloaded. This survey reviews twenty studies that bear on this problem, covering LLM-based programming assistance, eye tracking and gaze-aware assistants, facial-expression recognition of engagement and frustration, keystroke dynamics, and behavioral indicators of cognitive load. The literature shows that LLM feedback is generally well received and becomes more useful when it is tied to the student’s own code, that gaze reflects attention and comprehension effort, and that typing rhythm changes with emotional state and can be captured without a camera. However, most studies examine a single signal, rely on controlled or non-programming tasks, depend on self-reports, or target authentication rather than learning. From this synthesis we identify a gap: we found very little work that links learner-state sensing to LLM feedback in programming, and none that tests whether doing so improves learning. We outline a conceptual emotion-aware programming tutor as a research direction, kept separate from the reviewed evidence, and discuss privacy, bias, and evaluation challenges.

title_key: the role of leadership educators|guthrie
title: The Role of Leadership Educators
abstract:
Leadership, as a discipline; Leadership education, as a field; and Leadership educator, as a profession are rapidly evolving. As professionals in higher education, we are constantly asked to provide opportunities for students to learn leadership, whether that is inside or outside of the classroom. However, very little, if any professional development occurs in how to create such learning opportunities.
 The Role of Leadership Educators provides resources for leadership educators in three sections. The first section sets the stage for leadership education and the professional work of leadership educators, culminating with a variety of professional development resources for leadership educators. The second section introduces a leadership learning framework, provides characteristics and examples of strong leadership programs and assessment practices, and describes the transformative practice of leadership education.
 The third and final section offers specific instructional and assessment strategies ranging from discussion, case study, and reflection, to team-based- and service-learning to self-assessments, role-play, simulation, and games, to fulfill learning outcomes.
 This revised edition has been updated to include new topics such as program development and evaluation, as well as integration and application of generative Artificial Intelligence. Enhanced sections include leadership educator as a professional identity, learning contexts, and expanded coverage of instructional and assessment strategies. New examples and applications are offered throughout this second edition.

title_key: dampak pemanfaatan generative ai dalam meningkatkan kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis systematic literature review|dahlan
title: DAMPAK PEMANFAATAN GENERATIVE AI DALAM MENINGKATKAN KEMAMPUAN PEMECAHAN MASALAH MATEMATIS: SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
abstract: This research is systematic literature review aimed at knowing the impact of use generative artificial intelligence on enhancing the mathematical problem-solving abilities of students. Information search via Google Scholar (using the "Publish or Perish" tool) covering the period 2021 to 2026, with reporting conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Thought the selection process 15 articles were obtained to be analyzed. In mathematics learning the use of ChatGPT is most often used in solving problems.  The use of Generative AI enhances students’ skills in solving mathematical problems; however, its effectiveness is influenced by the students' existing mathematical proficiency. Although the benefits depend on students’ mathematical abilities, the use of generative AI generally leads to an improvement in students’ problem-solving skills. While Generative AI serves as a learning support tool, teachers retain a crucial role in providing guidance and facilitating exploration. A key challenge identified is the risk of over-reliance on Generative AI.
venue: PRISMATIKA Jurnal Pendidikan dan Riset Matematika

title_key: peers4u designing learner centered virtual peers for children s multimodal mathematics learning|zheng
title: Peers4U: Designing Learner-Centered Virtual Peers for Children's Multimodal Mathematics Learning
abstract: In early mathematics, children learn abstract concepts through concrete representations, such as manipulating objects, drawing, and speaking. Learning with peers can enrich this process by exposing children to diverse strategies and enabling them to exchange ideas through interaction. We realized this potential with virtual peers in Peers4U, a multimodal learning system to enhance children's mathematical conceptual understanding. Virtual peers driven by LLMs are personalized to the learner's cognitive level and assigned multimodal solutions with inspectable processes. During learning, peers engage in mixed-initiative interactions by responding, initiating topics, and advancing discussions along a pedagogical progression. A user study with 22 children and two experts showed our learner-centered topic orchestration significantly outperformed a persona-centered baseline, and children spontaneously authored new artifacts to demonstrate inspired ideas or share their own strategies, producing significantly more solutions when grouped with more Leading Peers. We contribute design insights for multimodal, learner-centered virtual peer systems.

title_key: communicative prompt functions and interactional engagement in chatgpt 4 assisted efl role play|anas
title: Communicative Prompt Functions and Interactional Engagement in ChatGPT-4-Assisted EFL Role-Play
abstract: This qualitative descriptive study examined the communicative functions of student-generated prompts in written ChatGPT-4-assisted role-play among third-semester EFL students. Fifteen third-semester students enrolled in the English Language Education Study Program at Sanata Dharma University, Indonesia, were selected through purposive sampling. The primary dataset consisted of transcripts of written role-play conversations; an open-ended reflective questionnaire was planned as a supplementary source. An analysis of selected conversational turns identified seven prompt functions: relational, self-disclosure, topic development, exploratory, affective support, reflective, and closing. The excerpts indicate that students used prompts to participate in simulated dialogue and influenced subsequent AI-generated turns. Requests for reasons and clarification illustrated inquiry-oriented actions, whereas contextually linked follow-up questions illustrated interactional continuity. These findings illustrate how student-generated prompts organize the initiation, continuation, and closure of AI-mediated written interactions.

title_key: prediksi ipk berdasarkan pola generative ai prompt engineering dan jam belajar menggunakan machine learning|amanda
title: Prediksi IPK Berdasarkan Pola Generative AI, Prompt Engineering, dan Jam Belajar Menggunakan Machine Learning
abstract:
Abstract. A Grade Point Average (GPA) estimated early helps institutions plan academic support, while the use of Generative AI among students keep growing with inconsistent evidence of its effect. This study aims to predict students’ post-semester GPA from Generative AI usage patterns, prompt engineering proficiency, and conventional study hours, and to compare the performance of LightGBM Regressor and Random Forest Regressor. The data are a synthetic Kaggle dataset of 50,000 students with 12 predictor variables, after variables that could cause data leakage were excluded. The data were split into training and test sets at an 80:20 ratio, and both models were trained as baselines and after hyperparameter tuning with RandomizedSearchCV, and validated with five-fold cross-validation. Performance was measured with MAE, MSE, RMSE, and R², while variable contributions were analyzed through feature importance, permutation importance, and ablation. The results show that the tuned LightGBM performed best, with an MAE of 0.1121, an RMSE of 0.1422, and an R² of 0.9162, slightly above Random Forest with an R² of 0.9084. Pre-semester GPA was the dominant predictor, contributing about 94% of gain-based importance. The three main study variables added only 0.0326 to R², so they act as complementary factors. 
  
Keywords: GPA prediction; Generative AI; prompt engineering; LightGBM; Random Forest 
  
Abstrak. Indeks Prestasi Kumulatif (IPK) yang dapat diperkirakan lebih awal membantu institusi merencanakan pendampingan akademik, sementara penggunaan Generative AI di kalangan mahasiswa terus meningkat dengan dampak yang belum seragam. Penelitian ini bertujuan memprediksi IPK mahasiswa setelah semester berjalan berdasarkan pola penggunaan Generative AI, kemahiran prompt engineering, dan jam belajar konvensional, serta membandingkan kinerja LightGBM Regressor dan Random Forest Regressor. Data yang digunakan adalah dataset sintetis dari Kaggle yang memuat 50.000 mahasiswa dengan 12 variabel prediktor setelah variabel yang berpotensi menimbulkan kebocoran data dikeluarkan. Data dibagi menjadi data latih dan data uji dengan rasio 80:20, kemudian kedua model dilatih pada kondisi baseline dan setelah penyetelan hiperparameter dengan RandomizedSearchCV, serta divalidasi silang lima lipatan. Kinerja diukur dengan MAE, MSE, RMSE, dan R2 sedangkan kontribusi variabel dianalisis melalui feature importance, permutation importance, dan ablation. Hasil menunjukan LightGBM setelah penyetelan hiperparameter memberikan kinerja terbaik dengan MAE 0,1121, RMSE 0,1422, dan R2 0,9162, sedikit di atas Random Forest dengan R2 0,9084. IPK sebelum semester menjadi prediktor yang paling dominan, dengan kontribusi sekitar 94% pada importance berbasis gain. Ketiga variabel utama penelitian hanya menambah R2 sebesar 0,0326, sehingga berperan sebagai faktor pelengkap.

title_key: inteligencia artificial generativa en la educacion media superior aplicaciones resultados desafios y consideraciones eticas una revision sistematica|zuniga
title: Inteligencia artificial generativa en la Educación Media Superior: aplicaciones, resultados, desafíos y consideraciones éticas. Una revisión sistemática
abstract: This systematic review examined the applications, outcomes, challenges, and ethical considerations of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in upper secondary education. Studies published between 2022 and August 2026 were searched in Google Scholar, SciELO, Redalyc, and Dialnet. The final corpus comprised 32 unique empirical studies, examined through an integrative qualitative synthesis. Applications included writing, language learning, mathematics, science, programming, tutoring, and feedback. Findings were heterogeneous, including positive, null, negative, and mixed outcomes. Perceived usefulness and AI-assisted performance do not necessarily indicate independent learning. Key challenges involved cognitive dependence, reliability, equity, academic integrity, and privacy. The educational potential of GenAI depends on pedagogical design and approaches that preserve learner autonomy and critical thinking. Further comparative studies assessing unassisted performance are needed to clarify its effects on learning.

title_key: making the invisible visible a framework for reflective ai use in software engineering education|shakiba
title: Making the Invisible Visible: A Framework for Reflective AI Use in Software Engineering Education
abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is increasingly embedded in software engineering education, supporting activities such as requirements development, design exploration, documentation, and prototyping. However, educators often have visibility only into final artefacts, with limited insight into how students evaluate, verify, and refine AI-generated outputs during the learning process. This creates challenges for assessing evaluative judgement and responsible AI-assisted practice. This paper introduces the AI Journal, a structured reflection framework designed to make student-GenAI interaction visible in first-year software engineering education. The framework combines execution tracking, which records prompts, outputs, intent, and interaction context, with cognitive auditing, which captures verification strategies, intervention decisions, confidence judgements, critical learning moments, and reflections on AI-supported work. Deployed in a first-semester software engineering course, the AI Journal enabled visibility into aspects of student learning not observable through artefact-based assessments alone. Preliminary observations suggested variation in verification practices, intervention strategies, and perceptions of AI-supported work. Critical learning moments frequently occurred when students evaluated contextual suitability, feasibility, and requirements alignment rather than identifying obvious errors. The AI Journal demonstrates a practical, lightweight, and model-agnostic approach for making AI-assisted learning processes visible. By foregrounding verification, intervention, and reflection, it shifts attention from product-focused assessment toward evaluative judgement and responsible AI-assisted practice.

title_key: an llm based motivational interviewing training system for japanese clinical education|arashi
title: An LLM-based motivational interviewing training system for Japanese clinical education
abstract: Abstract Background Motivational interviewing (MI) is an evidence-based approach for promoting behavior change in mental health, primary care, and public health. Effective MI training requires repeated practice with expert feedback, yet such resources remain scarce, and few tools support Japanese. Large language models (LLMs) offer scalable training, but whether LLM-based assessment agrees with expert evaluation remains largely unverified, particularly for Japanese. Methods We developed an LLM-based MI training system for Japanese clinical education and are validating its evaluation module against expert judgment. From book-derived case seeds, we generated 81 synthetic Japanese MI dialogues (27 scenarios x 3 intended counselor skill levels). The LLM evaluator assigns MITI 4.2.1 global scores (primary) and utterance-level behavior codes (secondary) with written rationales. Validation comprises (a) benchmarking against the official MITI 4.2.1 manual coding examples and (b) blinded coding of a held-out set by an expert rater, with a second expert reviewing uncertain judgments; agreement is assessed by intraclass correlation and weighted kappa. Results On 106 coding examples from the official MITI 4.2.1 manual, the evaluator achieved 71.7% accuracy (Cohen’s kappa=0.68), within the range of inter-coder agreement reported among trained human raters. Misclassifications concentrated in categories that also challenge human coders, such as simple versus complex reflections. Blinded expert coding of a held-out set is ongoing; agreement results will be presented at the conference. Conclusions Anchoring automated assessment to the official MITI standard and blinded expert judgment can make scalable MI training trustworthy for Japanese clinical education. Future work includes a feasibility pilot with medical students, strengthening workforce capacity for behavior change counseling. Key messages • An LLM-based system can provide scalable MI training for Japanese clinical education, addressing limited access to expert feedback and practice opportunities. • Anchoring LLM evaluation to official MITI benchmarks and blinded expert coding provides a transparent template for validating AI-assisted skills training before educational use.

title_key: hubungan pemanfaatan kecerdasan buatan ai sebagai sumber belajar dengan kemandirian belajar siswa pai di smp|wulandari
title: HUBUNGAN PEMANFAATAN KECERDASAN BUATAN (AI) SEBAGAI SUMBER BELAJAR DENGAN KEMANDIRIAN BELAJAR SISWA PAI DI SMP
abstract:
ABSTRACT
The use of generative artificial intelligence in education creates opportunities for students to access information and understand learning materials more flexibly. However, such accessibility does not necessarily correspond to students’ ability to manage their own learning independently, particularly in Islamic Religious Education (PAI) at the junior secondary school level. This study aims to examine the relationship between the use of ChatGPT as a learning resource and students’ learning independence at SMPN 5 Ambarawa. A quantitative approach with a correlational design was employed, involving 64 students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a four-point Likert-scale questionnaire measuring ChatGPT utilization and learning independence. The data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27 through descriptive statistics, instrument validity and reliability testing, and Spearman’s rho correlation analysis. The results revealed a positive and statistically significant relationship between ChatGPT utilization and students’ learning independence, with a correlation coefficient of 0.598 and a significance value of p < 0.001. These findings indicate that better utilization of ChatGPT tends to be associated with higher levels of learning independence. Nevertheless, this relationship does not establish a causal effect. The use of ChatGPT in Islamic Religious Education should therefore be accompanied by teacher guidance, information verification, and active student engagement to ensure that the technology is used critically and responsibly.
ABSTRAK
Pemanfaatan kecerdasan buatan generatif dalam pembelajaran membuka peluang bagi siswa untuk memperoleh informasi dan memahami materi secara lebih fleksibel. Namun, kemudahan akses tersebut belum tentu sejalan dengan kemampuan siswa mengelola proses belajarnya secara mandiri, khususnya dalam mata pelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) di jenjang sekolah menengah pertama. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan antara pemanfaatan ChatGPT sebagai sumber belajar dan kemandirian belajar siswa di SMPN 5 Ambarawa. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain korelasional yang melibatkan 64 siswa melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan angket skala Likert empat pilihan yang mengukur pemanfaatan ChatGPT dan kemandirian belajar. Data dianalisis menggunakan IBM SPSS Statistics versi 27 melalui statistik deskriptif, pengujian validitas dan reliabilitas instrumen, serta korelasi Spearman’s rho. Hasil analisis menunjukkan hubungan positif dan signifikan antara pemanfaatan ChatGPT dan kemandirian belajar siswa, dengan koefisien korelasi sebesar 0,598 dan nilai signifikansi p < 0,001. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa pemanfaatan ChatGPT yang lebih baik cenderung berkaitan dengan kemandirian belajar yang lebih tinggi. Meskipun demikian, hubungan tersebut tidak membuktikan sebab-akibat. Penggunaan ChatGPT dalam pembelajaran PAI perlu disertai bimbingan guru, verifikasi informasi, dan keterlibatan aktif siswa agar teknologi dimanfaatkan secara kritis dan bertanggung jawab.

title_key: assistant or ghostwriter eap instructors views on the opportunities and risks of genai in l2 writing|abdelmageed
title: Assistant or Ghostwriter? EAP Instructors’ Views on the Opportunities and Risks of GenAI in L2 Writing
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) systems are able to generate, revise and comment on second language (L2) student writing. However, less is known about where L2 writing teachers locate the opportunities and risks of such systems across the writing process. To that end, this study examined how English for academic purposes (EAP) writing instructors at two universities in Oman position GenAI within the L2 writing process. It focused on, first, the stages at which instructors locate GenAI's opportunities and risks, second, their views on GenAI as a source of feedback, and lastly their preparedness to manage academic integrity in AI-assisted L2 writing. A cross-sectional questionnaire combining Likert-scale items and open-ended prompts was completed by 51 EAP instructors , of whom 49 were retained for analysis. Closed items were analysed with descriptive statistics, Spearman correlations, McNemar tests and Mann–Whitney U tests. Open-ended responses were coded by writing stage through qualitative content analysis. The results showed that L2 writing instructors located GenAI's opportunities mainly in their own preparation of materials and model texts and in feedback. On the other hand, they highlighted its risks in students' drafting and in assessment. Revising and editing was contested, cited equally often as an opportunity and a risk. EAP instructors were more confident in using GenAI to prepare materials than in designing students' use of it at each writing stage. Just over half agreed that AI improves their feedback. This view was related to their overall attitude towards GenAI but not to their confidence as feedback providers. Most instructors felt responsible for checking students' GenAI use and confident in setting boundaries, but their confidence in maintaining academic integrity was unrelated to this sense of responsibility. More EAP instructors reported knowing how to use AI detectors than understanding how such detectors work. The study concludes that EAP instructors' readiness to integrate GenAI into L2 writing teaching and learning is uneven across the L2 writing process. Professional learning and development should therefore target the pedagogical design of student-facing AI use, the evaluation of AI feedback, AI detection literacy, and L2 writing assessment redesign.

title_key: data driven evaluation of ai tool specific impacts equity disparities and sustainable adoption framework for ai enhanced learning in pakistani higher education|ali
title: Data-Driven Evaluation of AI Tool-Specific Impacts, Equity Disparities, and Sustainable Adoption Framework for AI-Enhanced Learning in Pakistani Higher Education
abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming higher education, yet adoption in developing countries such as Pakistan remains constrained by limited empirical evidence, unequal access, and a lack of context-specific implementation frameworks. Existing Pakistani studies rely largely on self-reported perceptions from single urban regions, treat diverse AI tools as one category, and provide generalized recommendations without quantifiable impact analysis. This study proposes a data-driven, multi-region, twelve-month longitudinal evaluation of AI-enhanced learning across public and private universities in Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory. Using stratified random sampling, it distinguishes four tool classes: generative AI assistants, intelligent tutoring systems, NLP-based feedback tools, and predictive analytics platforms. Actual usage logs will be correlated with objective outcomes, including grade point averages, assessment scores, course completion rates, and retention metrics. The study will also examine disparities by gender, socioeconomic status, urban-rural location, and discipline, while evaluating risks of algorithmic bias, privacy breaches, and exclusion. Findings will inform a sustainable adoption framework comprising a cost-effective institutional implementation model, a tiered teacher-training roadmap, and a privacy- and ethics-compliant governance protocol aligned with Pakistan’s regulatory context. The study offers two contributions: a quantified, tool-specific evidence base on AI’s differential effects on teaching and learning, and a practical framework for policymakers and university leaders to scale AI integration equitably and sustainably. By connecting verified usage patterns with measurable outcomes across diverse institutions, the research moves beyond perception-based advocacy toward accountable, evidence-driven adoption in resource-constrained higher education systems while supporting accountability, educational quality, and inclusive digital transformation nationwide.

title: PERCEPÇÃO DOS ESTUDANTES DE TECNOLOGIA DA INFORMAÇÃO SOBRE O USO DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NO DESENVOLVIMENTO DE SOFTWARE: UM SURVEY NA UFERSA – CAMPUS PAU DOS FERROS
abstract: This study investigates how students enrolled in the Bachelor’s Degree in Information Technology (BTI) at the Federal Rural University of the Semi-Arid Region (UFERSA), Pau dos Ferros Campus, use and perceive Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools in learning and software development. The research was conducted through a structured survey comprising 18 questions, answered by 72 students. The instrument examined the frequency and purposes of AI use, the tools employed, practices for validating AI-generated responses and code, and participants’ perceptions of productivity, learning, autonomy, dependence, the job market, academic practices, and potential curricular adaptations. The results suggest that students perceive GenAI as a relevant tool for supporting learning and software development, while recognizing challenges related to autonomy, dependence, critical validation, and educational practices.

title_key: project based teaching in a deep learning course practice in a data science program at an application oriented university|zhang
title: Project-Based Teaching in a Deep Learning Course: Practice in a Data Science Program at an Application-Oriented University
abstract: Deep learning courses are conceptually abstract and involve a long engineering chain. Organized as lectures plus verification labs, they often leave students in an application-oriented data science program able to run code without being able to explain why a model works, and unable to transfer what they have practised to a new problem. This paper reports a project-based teaching practice in a 48-hour Deep Learning course. The content was reorganized into seven modules; instruction followed a path of problem-driven learning, knowledge construction and transfer; project tasks were arranged at four levels, from reproducing classic models to transfer, real application and final presentation; and five module assignments, one unit test and one project report carried the process assessment. A nine-step class procedure gave students about one third of the contact hours for self-study, group inquiry and coding. Over several rounds, project work was completed more often, topics moved from given datasets to real ones such as sheep breed recognition and leaf disease segmentation, and instructors spotted misunderstandings earlier by asking students to explain code on the spot. Limited contact hours, unclear individual contribution in group work and the assessment difficulty introduced by generative AI tools are also discussed.

title_key: microbiome science needs ai competence not just ai literacy|anand
title: Microbiome science needs AI competence, not just AI literacy.
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming embedded in microbiome research, yet the way microbiome scientists are trained has not kept pace. Existing discussions frequently emphasize AI literacy and responsible tool use. We argue that literacy alone is insufficient in a field where data leakage, incomplete metadata, ecological confounding, inappropriate model selection and unverified generative-AI outputs can produce convincing but biologically misleading conclusions. We propose an AI-competence framework comprising five connected capabilities: data and platform fluency, machine-learning competence, advanced model competence, large-language-model and agent competence, and biological closure. The final capability-the ability to connect computational predictions to independent data, mechanistic reasoning or experimental evidence-is essential for ensuring that predictive performance becomes meaningful biology. We further propose that competence should be demonstrated through reproducible scientific artifacts rather than course completion alone. Shared datasets, computational platforms and benchmark challenges could make such training broadly accessible while establishing common standards for evaluating AI competence in microbiome science.

title_key: university pharmacology students perspectives of and interactions with a course trained ai virtual tutor|kaur
title: University Pharmacology Students' Perspectives of and Interactions with a Course-Trained AI Virtual Tutor.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE
As generative AI use becomes widespread in pharmacology education, AI virtual tutors (AI-VTs) have the potential to offer personalized learning experiences. A course content-trained AI-VT was integrated into a large second-year undergraduate pharmacology course. The objectives of this work were to examine students' perceptions towards and student interactions with the AI-VT.


METHODS
Data were collected through a mixed-methods survey comprising Likert-type and open-ended questions, with responses stratified by students' self-reported use of the AI-VT (n=202). Open-ended responses were coded by multiple researchers and analyzed for recurring themes. Student conversations with the AI-VT were also analyzed to characterize usage patterns.


RESULTS
Student conversation data from AI-VT interactions showed evidence of iterative engagement and helped identify pharmacological concepts students found challenging. Students who used AI tools often prior to the course were more likely to engage with the AI-VT more regularly. Student perceptions of the AI-VT were generally positive with notable differences between user groups. Students who used the AI-VT frequently perceived a positive impact on their resilience, emotional support and academic performance. Student conversation data showed an increase in engagement with the AI-VT leading up to course exams. Students used the AI-VT for clarification on foundational concepts and as a tool to monitor their learning.


CONCLUSION
Integration of the course-trained AI-VT made for a positive student learning experience and provided insights into student usage patterns that can further inform AI-literacy initiatives. This work demonstrates a promising model for institutional integration of pedagogically-sound AI tools in pharmacology education and beyond.

title_key: the psychological effects of ai companions on loneliness and perceived social connection among young adults|nasir
title: The Psychological Effects of AI Companions on Loneliness and Perceived Social Connection Among Young Adults
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) companions are becoming more popular as conversational and emotional supports, but their association with loneliness and social connection among young adults in South Asia has not been extensively studied. The present study investigated the relationship between using AI companions, loneliness, and perceived social connection in young adults. The design employed was quantitative cross-sectional, involving 280 participants aged 18-30 years who have experienced using AI conversational companions like ChatGPT, Replika, or Character. The participants were AI who were recruited by purposive sampling. Loneliness was assessed using the UCLA Loneliness Scale, perceived social connection with the Social Connectedness Scale–Revised (SCS-R) and AI companion engagement with interaction frequency, emotional reliance, and perceived companionship items. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and hierarchical multiple regression (controlling for age, gender, and educational level) were used for data analysis. The results showed that greater loneliness was correlated with greater AI companion engagement (β = .38), while greater perceived social connection was correlated with less engagement (β = −.33); the latter correlated with greater engagement at the component level, whereas the former did not. The design was cross-sectional, giving the results that are compatible with the postulates of both displacement and compensation. They recommend that the quality of and emotional function of the use of AI should also be taken into account in student support and digital wellbeing campaigns, and not just the frequency of use.

title_key: exploring the direction of university ai education in the era of ai driven digital transformation focusing on generative ai use experiences and perceptions among learners in major courses at university a|kim
title: Exploring the Direction of University AI Education in the Era of AI-Driven Digital Transformation: Focusing on Generative AI Use Experiences and Perceptions among Learners in Major Courses at University A
abstract:
This study aims to provide implications for the direction of university AI education 
in the era of AI-driven digital transformation by analyzing the experiences and 
perceptions of generative AI use among learners in major courses at University A. To 
this end, a survey was conducted among learners enrolled in major courses at 
University A. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics for each 
i t em and trend analysis by domain, while open-ended responses were categorized and 
analyzed according to meaning units. The findings are as follows. First, students in 
both major courses used generative AI very frequently, mainly using ChatGPT, 
Gemini, and Claude. Second, students in the AI EduTech course showed higher levels 
of AI literacy, ethical and responsible awareness, and needs for university AI 
education than those in the startup course, while both groups perceived AI as useful 
for assignments. Third, the pre- and post-course analysis showed significant 
improvements in generative AI use, prompting competence, ethical understanding, 
and critical reconstruction attitudes in both courses. Fourth, the open-ended 
responses showed that students emphasized AI ethics, responsible use, prompt 
writing, assessment fairness, clear AI-use guidelines, and major-specific AI education. 
The findings are expected to serve as foundational data for developing 
university-level AI general education, discipline-linked AI curricula, AI use guidelines, 
and teaching and learning support systems

title_key: generative artificial intelligence assisted language learning cognitive mechanisms theoretical tensions and ethical governance|hao
title: Generative Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Language Learning: Cognitive Mechanisms, Theoretical Tensions, and Ethical Governance
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the environment of language learning, but its theoretical basis and ethical boundaries have not been fully explored. This paper builds a multi-level analytical system for AI-assisted language learning based on cognitive load theory, the zone of proximal development, generative linguistics and the technology acceptance model. AI can help students learn better by reducing extraneous cognitive load and providing easy-to-access support and instant correction; however, due to technological limitations, it may also reduce students' sense of ability and self-management. Generative linguistics and generative AI are not in opposition; rather, the former advocates for data frugality and innate mechanisms, while the latter is characterized by data maximalism and statistical learning; they are in harmony at the level of third factors and the Minimalist Program. According to the above research, chatbots have shown a modest positive effect on language learning; this degree varies depending on the learner's level, interface Design, interaction characteristics, etc. Based on the above, this paper introduces a "Smart Chinese" collaborative learning plugin that integrates ChatGPT with special scaffolding tools for assessment, planning, practice, feedback and community support. Finally, it presents the ethical problems of algorithmic bias, data privacy, over-reliance, and educational gaps, and proposes a multi-level governance system at the institutional, technological and pedagogical levels.

title_key: research on a vertical domain personalized learning system based on rag and multi agent collaboration|geng
title: Research on a Vertical-Domain Personalized Learning System Based on RAG and Multi-Agent Collaboration
abstract: Specialized courses frequently encounter fragmented knowledge resources, insufficient adaptation to individual learning needs, and delayed feedback. This work presents a personalized learning system for vertical domains that combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with a multi-agent framework. Learner profiles incorporate prior knowledge, learning goals, weak knowledge points, and preferred difficulty levels, while a domain-specific knowledge base supplies external retrieval content. During resource generation, retrieved knowledge and learner profile data jointly inform the production of reading materials, quizzes, practical tasks, and animation scripts. A review agent evaluates generated resources prior to learner delivery. Learning records—including quiz results, coding performance, task completion, and learning time—update learner profiles and guide subsequent resource and path adjustments. Experimental results show that the proposed system achieves better resource adaptability than direct LLM generation and supports personalized learning in vertical domains.
